user.title: OptoV
user.description: Pick the serial port wired to the controller's Optolink port; the serial proxies of your ESPHome nodes are listed there. For a node Home Assistant does not have, choose “Enter manually” and type its address.

data.language: Catalog language (names of datapoints and values)

manual.title: Connection details
manual.description: The address and API encryption key of an ESPHome node that Home Assistant does not have.

data.language: Catalog language (names of datapoints and values)
data.instance: Serial port on the node (0 unless it has several)
data.proxy_name: Serial proxy name (optional, distinguishes identical devices)

catalog.title: Controller catalog
catalog.description: OptoV needs a controller catalog. It is not shipped with the integration: you build it from your own copy of the controller service software with VExtractor, as described in the README under "The catalog". Choose one that is already here, or upload a new one.

reconfigure.title: Controller catalog
reconfigure.description: Choose another catalog for this controller, or upload a new build; the integration reloads with it. An upload with the name of a catalog already here replaces that file for every controller using it. Catalogs no controller uses can be ticked for deletion below.

error.cannot_connect: Could not connect to the ESPHome node.
error.catalog_invalid: That file is not a controller catalog.
error.catalog_failed: The catalog could not be installed. Check the Home Assistant log.
error.catalog_missing: Choose a catalog or upload one.
error.catalog_outdated: That catalog was built by an older version of the compiler than this integration needs. Rebuild it and upload it again.
error.catalog_too_new: That catalog was built by a newer version of the compiler than this integration understands. Update the integration.
error.catalog_in_use: Not deleted, still in use: {entries}. Switch those controllers to another catalog first.

abort.already_configured: This controller is already set up.
abort.reconfigure_successful: The catalog was changed. The integration reloads with it.

init.title: OptoV
init.description: Which datapoints become entities, and how the controller is polled. A group switched on here appears about 30 seconds after saving, when Home Assistant reloads the integration.

data.language: Catalog language (names of datapoints and values)
data.sync_clock: Keep the controller clock in sync with Home Assistant

catalog_missing.message: No controller catalog was found in {path}. The catalog is built from your own copy of the controller service software and is not shipped with the integration. Build one as described in the README section "The catalog" and upload it with Reconfigure on this entry.

catalog_gone.message: The controller catalog "{name}" is no longer in {path}. Put it back under that name, or choose another catalog with Reconfigure on this entry.

catalog_ambiguous.message: There is more than one controller catalog in {path} and this entry does not say which one to use. Choose it with Reconfigure on this entry.

catalog_outdated.message: The catalog "{name}" has structure version {found}; this integration needs {needed}. Rebuild it with the current VExtractor and upload it with Reconfigure on this entry.

catalog_too_new.message: The catalog "{name}" has structure version {found}, which is newer than the {needed} this integration understands. Update the integration.

catalog_unreadable.message: The catalog "{name}" could not be read as a controller catalog. Rebuild it and upload it with Reconfigure on this entry.

controller_unknown.message: The controller reports System ID {sys_id} with hardware index {hw} and software index {sw}. The catalog “{name}” has no entry for that: it describes {variants} for this System ID. Report these three values in a GitHub issue so the controller can be supported.

controller_protocol.message: This controller identifies itself as System ID {sys_id}, which this integration cannot drive over Optolink: the controllers behind those ids speak the older GWG protocol, whose addresses are a single byte, are reached over a two-wire bus rather than the optical port, or are described as OpenTherm data rather than as addresses. OptoV will not try: an address sent to any of them would land somewhere else rather than be refused.

no_controller.message: No OptoV controller is set up, so there is nothing to do this to.

which_controller.message: More than one controller is set up. Say which one the call is for.

unknown_schedule.message: No controller has a weekly programme called "{schedule}".

controller_refused.message: The controller refused {address} with error {code}. 0x01 means it does not have that address; 0x04 means the length does not match its own layout, so read the datapoint's whole block, not just its value.

card.title: Schedule
card.no_entity_hint: The OptoV integration publishes one schedule sensor per programme once it has been read from the controller.
card.faults_no_entity: No fault history found. The OptoV integration publishes one per controller.

text.catalog_option_outdated: built for an older version, rebuild it
text.catalog_option_too_new: newer than this integration, update the integration

dst_mismatch.title: Controller: daylight-saving settings
dst_mismatch.description:
The controller changes over at {configured}, but {zone} changes at {expected}. Each entry reads month/week/weekday, where week 5 means the last one of the month and weekday 7 is Sunday.

The clock itself is corrected on every poll, so the effect is limited to one poll interval twice a year. To fix it at the source, set the changeover values on the controller, or switch its own changeover off and let Home Assistant keep the time.

orphaned_statistics.title: Statistics of switched-off entities
orphaned_statistics.description:
{count} entities of {name} that this integration switched off, for example by lowering a tier, still have long-term statistics. Home Assistant keeps them so that an entity switched on again continues its history, and lists each of them on its statistics page until deleted.

Delete them here in one go, or leave them if you expect to switch the tier back on. Entities you disabled yourself are not included.

confirm.title: Delete statistics of switched-off entities
confirm.description: This deletes the long-term statistics of {count} entities that are currently switched off. Their history is gone for good; if one of them is switched on again later, it starts a new history.
